input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there

doc_friction.issue: 'pick the project that has gone longest without a new piece' is hard to apply: the git log shows only Hearth & Horizon commits (all three shelves live in one venture), so this run took the newest proposal in BIBLE.md 'Next up' instead.

overlap.mjs flagged Sicily, Nino and Concetta only after the setting was chosen; checking setting and names before planning would have saved a re-plan. The evaporative-cooler subject in subjects.txt overlaps 'The Pot That Needs Dry Air' (same wet-bulb, humid-week mechanism), but --unused still offers it.

deviations.why: The proposal suggested 'shade and wet curtains by day'. A wet curtain in a window that stays shut all day mostly adds moisture rather than cooling, so the story makes it a failed side trial and the note says why.
deviations.did: Wet sheet trial written as a 0.3 degree warmer result in an empty room.
deviations.result: The physics stays honest; the proposal's other beats were kept.

notes: Creative track, Hearth & Horizon shelf: new story 'The Square That Stays Warm' (slug the-square-that-stays-warm), text only because audio is 577 MB, over the 400 MB cap. About 5,100 words. The numbers come from a 10-minute-step model (fields, garden and square air; front and back rooms; shut, all-open-at-22:00, rule and windy nights), and every figure in the dialogue was checked against the closing note. The re-read caught: the facade orientation contradicting the shutter rule, a 1961 wedding dated before the speaker's 1956 birth, a room-number clash, and a claimed 'half a degree by morning' cost of waiting until 02:00 that the model put at 0.02. Weekdays and sunset (21:54 CEST) were computed. Sources: Oke 1973, Atmospheric Environment 7:769-779 (heat island vs log population and wind); Met Office tropical-night definition. Added a BIBLE timeline row and a new Listeria/soft-cheese proposal. node --test 20/20 pass; check_posts ok.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a researched 5,000-word short story with worked numbers, about two working days for a writer

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
